prompt:
A desktop landing page for sqwer, a free touch-typing course for beginners and schools, rendered edge to edge as a finished website screen with crisp readable text, no browser window, no device, no desk.

The page is built as a shallow suminagashi marbling basin: ultramarine and deep indigo ink floating in feathered currents on still porcelain-white water, the dye thinning to soft grey where it has spread, the newest drop always the darkest ring. The marbled surface is the page ground and fills most of the first viewport; a still, quiet margin holds the type.

What leads: in the calm centre of the swirl floats a single typing line in monospace, "f j f j  fj jf", and beneath each typed letter a fresh ring of ultramarine ink spreads into the current. In the still left margin, an elegant high-contrast serif headline: "Learn to type properly, one key at a time." and a quiet line: "Every key you type drops ink. Calm practice from your first two keys to fluent typing." A single ultramarine button: "Get started". Along the bottom of the basin, twelve small ink rings in a row, labelled "1 The home row", "2 Reaching up", "3 Reaching down", the first one dark and fresh.

Frame: the sqwer wordmark top left, navigation "Learn  Practice  Ranked", "Sign in" at the far right, all in a quiet humanist sans. Corners barely softened.
note: Free-plan watermark; no reference images attached (OpenArt upload would exceed credits); style described in the prompt.
